mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 9.0% signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 9.0%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in private employment (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals robust economic growth, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and RSAFS growth > 0.5%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90.0 (index) signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 90.0, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates a strengthening housing market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST is above its 1-year average, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening monetary policy in a strong labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening in a strong labor market
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS growth > 0.1% and UNRATE decline > 0.2%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high GDP growth (GDPC1 growth > 3.0% annualized), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overvaluation, leading to negative returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 growth > 3.0% annualized, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
